public_call_shape.ownership: Table is feature glue: TableEditing, TableUI, TableSelection, TableMouse, TableKeyboard, TableClipboard and Widget. TableColumnResize is absent from its requires list.

TableSelection computes cell membership, span bounds and range order; engine document selection owns the resulting ranges. Querying selected cells yields document/source order, while first/last selection ranges encode gesture anchor/focus.

Both command names register the same TableWidthsCommand instance. Options accept columnWidths as string[] or a comma-separated string; table defaults to the selected element. Omitting tableWidth removes it; omitting columnWidths removes the column group. These are reset semantics, not a partial update.

calls: editor.plugins.get( WidgetResize ).attachTo( { editor, modelElement, viewElement, unit: '%' /* or 'px' */, getResizeHost, getHandleHost, isCentered, onCommit } )
resizer.begin( domResizeHandle ); resizer.updateSize( mouseEvent ); resizer.commit(); resizer.cancel();
public_call_shape.ownership: WidgetResize/WidgetResizer own editing-view geometry and the gesture UI; the supplied onCommit callback owns feature-specific model persistence. The actual image adapter invokes editor.execute( 'resizeImage', { width: newValue } ), adds/removes image CSS and binds enablement.

calls: editor.execute( 'tableWidth', { value: '300px' } ) /* when table-properties command is installed */
public_call_shape.ownership: resizeTableWidth and resizeColumnWidths remain aliases. tableColumnWidth applies to columns covered by selected cells in a regular resized table; it accepts string/number and defaults numeric input to px. The table's width unit remains authoritative, so a px input is not itself a command to switch the whole table into pixel mode. The optional tableWidth command hook reconciles column units in the same batch.

findings.finding: CKEditor reuses generic model ranges/operations and the editing mapper. Tables own schema and domain semantics in a feature package. TableEditing separates editing conversions from data serialization; TableUI registers CKEditor UI components that call commands. This is not evidence that TableEditing is DOM-free: it installs editing converters, and TableColumnResizeEditing itself installs DOM listeners and UI handles.
findings.inference: Framework-neutral model behavior and rendering/input adapters are separable responsibilities; CKEditor plugin names alone do not establish that boundary.

findings.finding: setCellSelection writes one createRangeOn(cell) per chosen cell into model.document.selection with backward direction. Anchor/focus are the first/last ranges; membership and ordering are computed through TableWalker, including target colspan. DocumentSelection turns ranges into ModelLiveRange objects, and LiveRange transforms through document operations; removed ranges are detached from the selection. The integration assertion removes one selected row and retains the other row's two selected cells.
findings.inference: Generic range transformation earns core ownership; table rectangle/span semantics remain table-owned. A separate canonical selected-cell set in a UI store is unnecessary in this design.

findings.topic: View selection is a projection with explicit input adaptation
findings.finding: The editing downcast maps selected model cells to view elements, adds a highlight class, clears previous highlights, and places the actual view selection in the last selected cell. Typing replaces the incoming view selection with ranges for all selected model cells and prevents the browser default. TableMouse maps view positions into model cells, gates a cell drag until leaving the anchor cell, blocks selectionChange during the gesture, and clears local gesture references on mouseup.
findings.inference: Highlight and transient drag state belong to the editing/view adapter; delete/replace intent must still address model selection. The source comment describes browser normalization concerns, but this inspection provides no browser parity claim.

findings.finding: Copy/cut use TableSelection.getSelectionAsFragment to crop a standalone model table, preserve clipboard markers through shared utilities, and route serialized content through clipboardOutput. Cut is undoable and respects canEditAt. Table paste intercepts model insertion for table content, crops to target dimensions, repeats smaller source patterns using row/column modulo, trims spans and sets selection on inserted cells. Delete clears each selected cell's contents without deleting the cell shell, then collapses to the last source-order cell for backward deletion or the first for forward deletion.
findings.inference: A generic clipboard/selection transport cannot replace table paste geometry or content-clearing policy. These policies need a model-side table owner even if exposed by one public facade.

findings.finding: TableKeyboard uses localized arrow directions, table slots and span dimensions to navigate or extend selections. Shift expansion calls the same setCellSelection API as mouse selection. Reaching an outer boundary can select the whole table. Tab navigation relies on generic widget handling, while TableKeyboard adds a row through insertTableRowBelow at the last cell; tests assert final-row Tab creates and enters a new row.
findings.inference: Generic key dispatch/navigation support can be reused; table geometry and append-row policy cannot be deleted merely because dispatch is shared.

findings.topic: Column resize is not a WidgetResize client
findings.finding: TableColumnResizeEditing imports its own table utilities/command/observer and requires TableEditing and TableUtils; it does not attach a WidgetResizer. It keeps one plugin-local active gesture and geometry record, inserts column-edge UI elements in editing downcast, and listens to document mouse events. WidgetResize instead registers per-widget resizers keyed by view elements and renders four corner handles.
findings.inference: CKEditor's actual reusable resize API does not eliminate table-specific implementation. Similar begin/update/commit phases establish possible mechanical reuse, not a single proven geometry abstraction.

findings.finding: Mousedown validates resize allowance and model editability, stores the initial event, and starts the gesture after a horizontal distance threshold. The gesture measures DOM cells through model/view mapping, creates temporary view colgroup markup when necessary, and changes only editing-view widths during preview. Mouseup compares view widths with model values and commits through resizeTableWidth when allowed. If allowance was revoked, it restores existing widths or removes temporary colgroup/width/classes; it then removes active styling and clears active gesture data. Plugin destruction stops its DOM emitter.
findings.inference: Preview is intentionally local to the view; committed widths are model data. Read-only/disabled rollback is table-specific restoration of derived markup. These reads do not establish arbitrary cancellation or model-removal-during-drag correctness.

findings.topic: Table geometry survives any gesture-substrate extraction
findings.finding: An interior column edge transfers width between neighboring columns. The outer edge changes whole-table width, bounded by parent width; both use minimum column constraints. RTL changes the delta sign, centered outer-edge resizing doubles it, and layout tables do not inherit the normal table's implicit center alignment. TableWalker maps a spanned cell to its logical column edge. The model post-fixer adjusts width entries after insert/remove operations and normalizes percentages.
findings.inference: A reusable pointer transaction cannot decide neighbor redistribution, spans, layout alignment defaults, structural width repair or serialization. Moving these into a generic core would move table policy, not remove it.
findings.snapshot_caveat: Percentage-only normalization and the unconditional container clamp describe the old snapshot. CK-F12 records current pixel mode and an optional TableScroll-dependent overflow path.

findings.finding: The optional column-resize feature extends the model with table.tableWidth and a tableColumnGroup containing tableColumn.columnWidth (plus temporary colSpan import data). TableWidthsCommand writes these in model.change; conversion maps them to table/figure width styles and colgroup/col widths. Percentage normalization is table-owned; resized-table CSS uses fixed table layout. TableLayoutEditing reuses TableColumnResize, adds tableType and layout-specific schema rules. Its import test asserts tableType=layout, tableWidth=30%, and three persisted column widths. TableCellWidthEditing separately supplies per-cell tableCellWidth conversion/command.
findings.inference: Layout reuses a table-owned width model, not a generic widget-size attribute. Neither persistent widths nor layout meaning belongs solely to UI state.
findings.snapshot_caveat: The snapshot already accepts tableWidth strings such as 500px, but its drag path emits percentage table/column widths. Do not read this as a claim that current CKEditor only stores percentages; see CK-F12.

findings.finding: WidgetResizer creates fresh geometry state on begin, previews a single view-element width, and preserves aspect ratio using corner geometry. commit restores the initial view width, then invokes onCommit in the same view change; a no-proposal commit is suppressed. cancel restores the preview width and dismisses the size UI; destroy calls cancel. WidgetResize removes/destroys view-keyed resizers when their view element detaches, destroys retained resizers and stops listeners on teardown, and toggles the optional widget toolbar during begin/cancel/commit. Tests inspect rollback and registry removal after deletion or rerender.
findings.inference: A shared view-lifetime owner and preview/commit contract are credible reuse candidates. However cancel() itself only cleans the preview; the coordinator clears _activeResizer on mouseup. The inspected test does not prove cancel-then-mouseup suppresses commit, so do not promote a stronger universal cancellation guarantee.

findings.topic: Handle cardinality, hit testing and shared preview
findings.finding: Both revisions create one div.ck-table-column-resizer inside every editing-view table cell in the insert:tableCell downcast. This is one handle per actual rendered cell, not one table overlay and not one handle per logical column. For an unmerged R-by-C table the source implies R*C handles. Tests assert 4 on initial table insertion, 9 after extending a 2-by-3 table with a row, and 7 after splitting one of six cells. There are no bottom/row-height or extra first-column-start handles in this inserter. CSS places the single handle on the physical right border in LTR, left in RTL. On hover the same cell-owned handle is extended vertically to the table's full height using table/cell rect differences; mouseout removes that extension unless a resize is active. The extension does not replace the per-cell handles with a shared overlay.

hit_testing.owner: TableColumnResizeEditing's delegated view listeners plus browser CSS hit testing.
hit_testing.mechanism: Mouseover/mousedown test the event target's ck-table-column-resizer class; mousedown maps its figure ancestor to the model table and checks canEditAt. Resize-data construction maps the handle's td/th ancestor to the model cell, then TableUtils chooses its logical right edge, accounting for spans. Drag updates use document mousemove/mouseup. There is no nearest-edge scan or single-overlay edge picker in these inspected methods.

findings.preview_owner: One active gesture in the TableColumnResizeEditing plugin instance; the active table and column view elements are captured in _resizingData. Current resizingTable explicitly exposes the one table being resized. Per-cell handle count and shared preview ownership are separate decisions.
findings.inference: CKEditor corroborates per-cell handles with centralized gesture policy, not a one-overlay design. Relative to the lead-reported copied controls, CKEditor supplies evidence for one column-edge handle per cell. It does not establish equivalence for row-height resizing or justify deleting bottom handles without the lead's local requirement comparison.
findings.local_comparison_limit: Lead supplied: copied TableCellResizeControls mounts bottom+right per cell plus left on first-column, with table-owned preview. This worker did not inspect or validate that local implementation.

findings.topic: Fresh width contract: px and percent with the same table-owned lifecycle
findings.finding: Remote HEAD supports pixel table/column resizing. tableWidth ending in px selects pixel gesture mode; missing/non-pixel table width selects percentage mode. A pixel table may initially retain percentage columns from imported content. Drag preview writes px or % according to table mode; pixel commit resolves untouched percentage columns against the pre-drag table width, preserving their absolute widths, then writes a consistent pixel group. Percentage normalization still sums to 100%; the generic normalizer preserves pixel values instead of applying that invariant. The table post-fixer additionally handles pixel column totals. Changing tableWidth through its user command reconciles units in the same undo batch. These policies are all in the table feature.

contract_difference.snapshot: 48.0.1 snapshot tableWidth can already contain px, but the column drag seeds/previews/commits percentages; column upcast accepts %/pt and falls back to auto for px. Its column normalizer always emits percentages.
contract_difference.current_remote: 48.5.1 remote source preserves px columns when the table is pixel-sized and commits gestures in px. It also exposes tableColumnWidth and removes obsolete per-cell widths when column widths are set.

findings.additional_policy_observed: The remote drag path checks optional TableScrollEditing to permit container overflow, change centered-edge growth across the container boundary, and apply snap/resistance. Its broader implementation and tests were not audited. This further demonstrates feature-owned policy rather than a generic single-widget resize contract.
findings.inference: The ownership conclusion survives the freshness correction, but 'all widths must total 100%' must be qualified to percentage mode. Pixel totals, unit reconciliation, import rules and pre-drag conversion are additional table invariants, not generic WidgetResize policy.

promotion_and_cut.status: Bounded recommendation for lead comparison; not a local verdict or implementation proposal.
promotion_and_cut.strongest_justified_cut: Cut the assumption that a generic resize substrate can own or replace table column policy. Keep grid selection, span traversal, clipboard geometry and persisted width invariants with the table feature; reuse existing core range transformation instead of adding a parallel authoritative cell-selection store.
promotion_and_cut.strongest_justified_promotion: Promote the ownership rule that gesture preview is ephemeral view state and durable widths change only through the feature's model commit. If independent callers justify shared machinery, restrict it to gesture/view lifecycle and callback delivery; a single-widget aspect-ratio resizer is not a table layout engine.
promotion_and_cut.counterargument: CKEditor duplicates document mouse routing, geometry capture and cleanup across table and widget resize; a smaller common transaction/lifetime helper could reduce that duplication. Existing separation does not prove extraction is impossible, and the widget implementation itself carries image-like geometry assumptions. Any extraction still needs a table policy adapter and proof of cancellation/invalidation; this repository alone does not justify a new Plite core owner. Current upstream also retains per-cell handles despite one shared active resize; it cannot be cited as evidence for replacing all handles with a single overlay.
promotion_and_cut.adoption_constraint: Preserve this as external evidence. Lead must compare existing Plite/Plate owners and current user jobs before accepting a cut or promotion.

rejected_ideas.idea: Use WidgetResize unchanged for table column edges.
rejected_ideas.reason: Its public contract commits one width for one view element and its internal geometry assumes corner handles/aspect ratio; table edges redistribute neighbors and maintain a logical grid.

rejected_ideas.idea: Treat cell selection as DOM highlights or independent UI-only selected-cell state.
rejected_ideas.reason: Delete, typing, copy and paste depend on model ranges; engine range transformation preserves remaining selections across row removal.

rejected_ideas.idea: Move all table selection/clipboard semantics into generic selection core.
rejected_ideas.reason: Generic ranges do not determine span closure, rectangular extraction, repeated paste or neighbor navigation.

rejected_ideas.idea: Persist every resize move as a model change.
rejected_ideas.reason: Both implementations preview in the editing view and commit through a feature callback/command. Table source explicitly reserves preview from the shared model.

rejected_ideas.idea: Copy CKEditor's two width command names as independent capabilities.
rejected_ideas.reason: They are compatibility aliases to one command and share enablement; issue 12148 is closed NOT_PLANNED, not a separate-policy implementation.

rejected_ideas.idea: Claim cancel(), detached-view cleanup, or a closed issue proves all active-gesture invalidation works.
rejected_ideas.reason: Inspected tests cover specific rollback and registry cases, not complete Escape/pointercancel/concurrent deletion/cancel-then-mouseup behavior.

rejected_ideas.idea: Infer one table overlay from one shared resize-preview owner.
rejected_ideas.reason: Both local snapshot and current remote source create a handle in every cell. Hover extends that handle across the table; gesture state remains centralized.

rejected_ideas.idea: Treat current CKEditor table width persistence as percentage-only.
rejected_ideas.reason: That characterizes the old drag path, not current remote source. Current tableWidth selects px/% mode and tests assert persistent pixel columns after import and drag.

keyboard.observed: TableKeyboard selection/navigation is evidenced in CK-F05. The inspected table-column resize listener setup registers mouse events and its handle is a plain div with only a class. No resize-keyboard or Escape behavior was observed in these methods.
keyboard.limit: This is a bounded observation, not a product-wide absence claim or keyboard accessibility verdict.

rtl.observed: CSS moves the same cell-edge handle to the left and unsets right; drag math flips horizontal movement using the content direction. Snapshot Arabic-language test assertions cover shrinking the first column by dragging right.
rtl.limit: Source and tests inspected only; no live RTL/browser proof.

read_only_and_cancel.observed: Resize allowance combines editor read-only, feature enabled and command enabled states. Mousedown also requires model.canEditAt(table). Revocation routes the next active move to mouseup cancellation; mouseup restores model-derived view widths/removes temporary markup and clears gesture state. Disabled CSS hides handles. Generic WidgetResizer.cancel restores initial width but is not proven to abort every future coordinator event.
read_only_and_cancel.limit: No pointercancel/touch/Escape or concurrent-removal guarantee inferred.
